original_value: Alzheimer’s disease is an incurable neurodegenerative disease primarily affecting the elderly population. Efficient automated techniques are needed for early diagnosis of Alzheimer’s. Many novel approaches are proposed by researchers for classification of Alzheimer’s disease. However, to develop more efficient learning techniques, better understanding of the work done on Alzheimer’s is needed. Here, we provide a review on 165 papers from 2005 to 2019, using various feature extraction and machine learning techniques. The machine learning techniques are surveyed under three main categories: support vector machine (SVM), artificial neural network (ANN), and deep learning (DL) and ensemble methods. We present a detailed review on these three approaches for Alzheimer’s with possible future directions.

result.paraphrase: Alzheimer’s disease is an incurable neurodegenerative disorder that mainly affects older adults. Efficient automated methods are required for its early diagnosis, and researchers have proposed many new approaches for Alzheimer’s classification. However, developing more effective learning techniques requires a better understanding of prior Alzheimer’s research. In this review, we examine 165 papers published from 2005 to 2019 that use various feature extraction and machine learning methods. The machine learning techniques are organized into three major groups: support vector machine (SVM), artificial neural network (ANN), and deep learning (DL) and ensemble methods. We offer a detailed review of these three Alzheimer’s approaches, along with potential future directions.
